title: Kitchen hardware, construction and installation
intro: Create a coordinated manufacturing package that connects carcass details, hardware, site conditions and an inspectable installation sequence.
goals: Link hardware to units and parts

sections.title: Freeze the manufacturing references
sections.text: Reconcile plans, elevations, sections, cut lists, appliances and hardware by compatible revisions. Distinguish carcass, finished-part and cutting dimensions according to edge details. Mark unresolved device/service inputs and do not release affected parts as fully approved.
sections.caption: A release identifies its references and open items.

sections.title: Link hardware to units and parts
sections.text: For each hardware item record product code, handing, quantity, cabinet and approved drilling reference. Distinguish a purchased set from its component parts to avoid double ordering. Product changes reopen front, carcass, machining and motion coordination before procurement.
sections.caption: A set and its components are different counting units.

sections.title: Sequence installation and inspection
sections.text: Link site readiness to delivery and assembly of units, worktops and devices under their references. Put hold points before fixing/services are concealed and assign inspectors. Check alignment, operation and samples, then record corrections and reinspection; do not improvise load tests.
sections.caption: Acceptance of hidden work precedes concealment.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: The schedule orders a complete pull-out set and accidentally reorders its included components. Check the set contents, separate genuine additions and correct procurement.
example.decision: Decision: reconcile the purchasing unit before ordering.

quiz.question: How do you prevent double ordering set components?
options: Check set contents and purchasing units
quiz.explanation: Quantity must match the product actually supplied.

assignment.prompt: Submit an assembly detail, hardware schedule and installation plan with three inspection hold points and open items.
fields: Link hardware to units and parts

faq.question: Is a final elevation enough to manufacture?
faq.answer: No. Parts, details, hardware, references, service coordination and inspection points are also needed.
